title: Atelier
when: Fashion, craft, interiors, food and culture told like a magazine feature: a didone on porcelain paper, slow zooms, iris reveals and lower-third titles

voice.style: low, intimate, unhurried, like a magazine profile read aloud

rules: Statements are short and set large in the didone; the feeling word is its italic, never a colour alone. Leave two thirds of the frame empty around them.
Scene titles sit as lower thirds under the picture, the way a magazine captions a photograph.
Pictures are materials: a fabric, a surface, a plate (depth plates, duotone treatment) or one drawn object with a soft shadow. Nothing glossy, no neon, no outlines.
Move like a slow lens: zoom in on a detail, iris to the next, never whip or push. One scene per sentence; let silences hold on the picture.
Figures are set small in Inter under the didone headline, with their source, the way a caption credits a photograph.
